target: Обязательно позвони бабушке, она очень ждёт.
english: Make sure to call grandma, she's really waiting.

target: Объясните мне это правило ещё раз.
english: Explain this rule to me one more time.

target: Включите компьютер и откройте эту программу.
english: Turn on the computer and open this program.

target: Архитектор моет посуду дома после обеда.
english: The architect washes dishes at home after lunch.
grammar: Дома = at home. После обеда = after lunch (после + genitive). Мыть посуду = to wash dishes (imperfective).

target: Те, кто опоздал, не получат билеты.
english: Those who are late will not get tickets.
grammar: Где can replace в котором for locations: город, где я живу = the city where I live.

target: Если бы ты спросил, я бы ответил.
english: If you had asked, I would have answered.

target: В другой ситуации она бы поступила иначе.
english: In a different situation she would act differently.
grammar: Если бы + past tense = 'if' in unreal conditions: Если бы я знал...

target: Иди сюда и помоги мне переставить мебель.
english: Come here and help me rearrange the furniture.
grammar: Perfective imperatives for single completed actions: Открой окно! Open the window!

target: Приготовь завтрак, пока я собираюсь на работу.
english: Make breakfast while I get ready for work.
grammar: Приготовь is perfective imperative (informal): cook/prepare (one specific meal). Пока = while — for simultaneous actions.

target: Вымой руки перед едой, это очень важно.
english: Wash your hands before eating, it's very important.

target: Этот дом такой же большой, как тот.
english: This house is as big as that one.
grammar: Такой же...как = 'the same as/just as': такой же большой, как тот. This compares equality, not superlative degree.

target: Магазин, в котором я покупаю продукты, рядом.
english: The store where I buy groceries is nearby.
grammar: Что can mean 'that/which' for things: Всё, что я знаю = Everything that I know.

target: Выключи свет перед тем как выйти из комнаты.
english: Turn off the light before leaving the room.

target: Если бы он был здесь, он бы всё объяснил.
english: If he were here, he would explain everything.

target: Если бы у неё было время, она бы читала больше.
english: If she had time, she would read more.

target: Было бы хорошо поехать на море.
english: It would be nice to go to the sea.
grammar: Давай/Давайте + infinitive means 'let's': Давайте пойдём! (Let's go!).

target: Тот, кто много читает, много знает.
english: The one who reads a lot knows a lot.
grammar: Что can mean 'that/which' for things: Всё, что я знаю = Everything that I know.

target: Комната, в которой стоит пианино, большая.
english: The room in which the piano stands is big.

target: Если бы было тепло, мы бы гуляли.
english: If it were warm, we would take a walk.

target: Пиши аккуратно и не забывай проверять ошибки.
english: Write neatly and don't forget to check for mistakes.
grammar: Пожалуйста makes imperatives polite: Скажите, пожалуйста... Please tell me...

target: Позвони мне, когда вернёшься домой с работы.
english: Call me when you get back home from work.

target: Поздравь коллегу с повышением, он это заслужил.
english: Congratulate your colleague on the promotion, he deserved it.
grammar: Genitive plural has many endings: -ов/-ев (столов), -ей (ночей), zero ending (книг, мест).

target: Подготовь документы для завтрашней встречи с клиентом.
english: Prepare the documents for tomorrow's meeting with the client.

target: Напишите своё имя и фамилию в этой форме.
english: Write your first and last name on this form.
grammar: Напишите is formal plural imperative of написать (perfective). Своё имя и фамилию = your name and surname (accusative).

target: Выключите свет перед тем, как уйти из комнаты.
english: Turn off the light before you leave the room.
grammar: Из means 'from/out of': из дома (from the house), из России (from Russia).

target: Уберите со стола и помойте посуду после ужина.
english: Clear the table and wash the dishes after dinner.

target: Не трогай эту вазу, она очень старая и хрупкая.
english: Don't touch that vase, it's very old and fragile.

target: Если бы я был на твоём месте, я бы согласился.
english: If I were in your place, I would agree.
grammar: Бы can be placed after the verb or after the subject: Я бы хотел / Я хотел бы.

target: Если бы я умел петь, я бы спел для тебя.
english: If I could sing, I would sing for you.

target: Если бы у нас был сад, мы бы выращивали овощи.
english: If we had a garden, we would grow vegetables.

target: Карта мира висит на стене класса.
english: A map of the world hangs on the classroom wall.
grammar: На стене = on the wall (prepositional for location). Висит means 'is hanging.' Карта мира = map of the world (мира is genitive of мир).

target: Говорите медленнее, я не успеваю записывать.
english: Speak slower, I can't keep up with writing it down.

target: Продавец танцует вальс в библиотеке после обеда.
english: The salesman dances a waltz in the library after lunch.
grammar: В библиотеке = in the library. После обеда = after lunch. Танцевать вальс = to dance a waltz (imperfective).

target: Если бы он учился, он бы сдал экзамен.
english: If he had studied, he would have passed the exam.
grammar: The conditional is formed with past tense + бы: Я бы пошёл = I would go.

target: Если бы ты пришёл раньше, мы бы успели.
english: If you had come earlier, we would have made it.

target: Возьми зонт с собой, обещают дождь после обеда.
english: Take an umbrella with you, they promise rain after lunch.

target: Проверьте свои ответы ещё раз перед сдачей работы.
english: Check your answers one more time before submitting the work.

target: Не торопись, у нас ещё достаточно времени до начала.
english: Don't hurry, we still have enough time before the start.

target: Не сдавайтесь, успех приходит к тем кто не отступает!
english: Don't give up, success comes to those who don't retreat!

target: Звук гитары слышен из соседней комнаты.
english: The sound of a guitar is heard from the next room.
grammar: Из + genitive: из соседней комнаты = from the neighboring room. Звук гитары = sound of the guitar (genitive for possession).

target: Выберите блюдо из меню, официант скоро подойдёт.
english: Choose a dish from the menu, the waiter will come soon.
grammar: Пожалуйста makes imperatives polite: Скажите, пожалуйста... Please tell me...

target: Мы бы не заблудились, если бы взяли карту.
english: We wouldn't have gotten lost if we had taken a map.

target: Подожди меня здесь, я скоро вернусь из магазина.
english: Wait for me here, I'll be back from the store soon.

target: Объясни мне правила этой игры, я не понимаю.
english: Explain the rules of this game to me, I don't understand.

target: Собери вещи, мы уезжаем через час на дачу.
english: Pack your things, we're leaving for the dacha in an hour.
grammar: Perfective imperatives for single completed actions: Открой окно! Open the window!

target: Верни книгу в библиотеку до конца этой недели.
english: Return the book to the library by the end of this week.
Remember this rule!
grammar: Запомни is perfective imperative (informal): memorize/remember (this specific rule). Это правило = this rule (accusative neuter).

english: Remember my number!
Check the homework!
grammar: Проверь is perfective imperative (informal): check (one specific thing). Домашнюю работу = homework (accusative feminine).

english: Put things here!
Let's finish work!
The smallest kitten.
grammar: Всего/всех for superlative: Он лучше всех = He is the best of all.

english: Your ticket, please.
grammar: Ваш agrees with билет (masculine): ваш билет = your ticket. Пожалуйста here means 'please' in a polite request.

english: Let's try again!
grammar: Many prepositions take genitive: из (from), от (from), до (until), без (without), для (for).

english: Show me the way!
Whose notebooks are these?
Take documents with you!
Better late than never.
She is the best teacher.
The weather is getting warmer.
Work is becoming more interesting.
grammar: Some comparatives are irregular: хороший → лучше, плохой → хуже, большой → больше.

english: This is much more interesting.
grammar: Гораздо intensifies comparatives: гораздо интереснее = much more interesting. It has no equivalent in simple comparative form.

english: Family is the most precious.
grammar: Чем introduces comparison: Он старше, чем я = He is older than me.

english: She sings louder than everyone.
She is the kindest friend.
It's interesting with our teacher.
He became stronger after training.
grammar: Стал + comparative = became more: стал сильнее. Стать + comparative expresses change. После тренировок = after training (genitive plural).

english: Their house has three rooms.
grammar: Его (his), её (her), их (their) do NOT change form regardless of the noun's gender or case.

english: Moscow is bigger than St. Petersburg.
She is younger than her brother.
Friends are more important than work.
Time is more valuable than gold.
grammar: Ценнее is comparative of ценный (valuable). Золота is genitive — genitive replaces чем: ценнее золота = more valuable than gold.

english: The beauty of nature inspires artists.
grammar: Numbers 2-4 take genitive singular: два стола, три книги.

english: He is taller than his brother.
This house is bigger than ours.
She is stronger than she looks.
grammar: Some comparatives are irregular: хороший → лучше, плохой → хуже, большой → больше.

english: He is kinder than his father.
This is the most interesting task.
He is a more experienced doctor.
grammar: Более + adjective = compound comparative: более опытный = more experienced. Used when simple -ее comparative doesn't exist.

english: She is a less strict teacher.
The new apartment is more spacious.
He is much older than me.
grammar: Some comparatives are irregular: хороший → лучше, плохой → хуже, большой → больше.

english: He is not at all worse.
grammar: Ничуть не + comparative = not at all (worse): ничуть не хуже. Ничуть is an emphatic negation particle.

english: The eldest brother is the tallest.
He is younger than he looks.
My brother is older than me.
My father works as a doctor.
grammar: Чей/чья/чьё/чьи means 'whose': Чья это книга? Whose book is this?

english: The child paints a picture tomorrow.
He speaks Russian better than me.
grammar: Лучше is irregular comparative of хороший. Меня is genitive — genitive replaces чем: лучше меня = better than me.

english: The fastest train in the country.
grammar: Самый быстрый is superlative: the fastest. Самый + adjective. В стране = in the country (prepositional for location).

english: The oldest church in the city.
The newest building on the street.
grammar: Самое новое: самое is neuter superlative agreeing with здание (neuter). На улице = on the street (prepositional).

english: He speaks Russian better and better.
My favorite book is this one.

target: Сядьте поудобнее, мы начинаем нашу презентацию.
english: Sit comfortably, we're starting our presentation.

target: Держи меня в курсе дела по этому проекту.
english: Keep me updated on this project.
The soup is hotter than the porridge.
The train is slower than the plane.
She is more serious than her friend.
She is more beautiful than her sister.
This movie is better than that one.
grammar: Лучше is irregular comparative of хороший. Того is genitive demonstrative — genitive replaces чем: лучше того = better than that one.

english: This river is wider than that one.
She draws more beautifully than her friend.
grammar: Который (who/which/that) introduces relative clauses and declines by case.

english: The youngest sister is the most cheerful.
grammar: Всего/всех for superlative: Он лучше всех = He is the best of all.

english: He is more cheerful than his friend.
grammar: Чем introduces comparison: Он старше, чем я = He is older than me.

english: This city is cleaner than that one.
His office is farther from the metro.
The most delicious dish on the menu.
grammar: Самое вкусное: самое is neuter superlative agreeing with блюдо (neuter). В меню = in the menu (indeclinable loanword).

english: She is less capricious than her sister.
The weather is getting worse and worse.
grammar: Some comparatives are irregular: хороший → лучше, плохой → хуже, большой → больше.

target: Расскажите о своём путешествии в Петербург.
english: Tell me about your trip to Petersburg.

target: Он такой же высокий, как брат.
english: He is as tall as his brother.
grammar: Такой же + adjective + как = the same as: такой же высокий, как брат. This expresses equality of comparison, not superlative.

target: Расскажи мне о своём путешествии по Европе.
english: Tell me about your trip around Europe.
grammar: Расскажи is perfective imperative (informal): tell (a specific story). О + prepositional: о своём путешествии = about your trip.

target: Одевайся теплее, на улице мороз минус двадцать.
english: Dress warmly, it's minus twenty degrees outside.

target: Самый большой город в России — Москва.
english: The biggest city in Russia is Moscow.
grammar: Самый большой = the biggest (superlative). В России = in Russia (prepositional). Москва is in apposition — a clarifying noun.

target: Попробуй этот пирог, бабушка его только что испекла.
english: Try this pie, grandma just baked it.
A bicycle is more eco-friendly than a car.
She is a little younger than her sister.
grammar: Немного + comparative = 'a little (more)': немного моложе = a little younger. Сестры is genitive — genitive replaces чем.

english: This lesson is simpler than the previous one.

target: Покажите мне дорогу до центральной площади.
english: Show me the way to the central square.

target: Журналист всегда поёт песню в школе.
english: The journalist always sings a song at school.
grammar: Всегда (always) signals habitual action. Петь песню = to sing a song. В школе = in the school (prepositional).

target: Он бегает быстрее всех в классе.
english: He runs faster than everyone in the class.

target: Идите прямо по этой улице до перекрёстка.
english: Go straight down this street to the intersection.

target: Давайте поговорим о планах на следующий отпуск.
english: Let's talk about plans for the next vacation.
grammar: Давайте + perfective: давайте поговорим = let's talk (specific occasion). О + prepositional: о планах = about plans.

target: Позаботьтесь о домашних животных, пока меня нет.
english: Take care of the pets while I'm away.

target: Чем дальше в лес, тем больше дров.
english: The further into the forest, the more firewood.

target: Оденься теплее, на улице мороз и сильный ветер.
english: Dress warmer, it's freezing with strong wind outside.

target: Не сдавайся, ты уже почти достиг своей цели!
english: Don't give up, you've almost reached your goal!
grammar: Imperative for ты: verb stem + -й/-и: читай, пиши, говори.

target: Программист всегда убирает квартиру в музее.
english: The programmer always cleans the apartment in the museum.
grammar: Всегда (always) signals habitual action. Убирать квартиру = to clean the apartment. В музее = in the museum.

target: Книга, которую я читаю, очень интересная.
english: The book that I am reading is very interesting.
grammar: Которую is accusative feminine of который, agreeing with книга and functioning as direct object: книгу, которую я читаю.

target: Будьте добры, передайте мне соль и перец.
english: Be so kind, pass me the salt and pepper.
grammar: Пожалуйста makes imperatives polite: Скажите, пожалуйста... Please tell me...

target: Не волнуйся, всё будет хорошо после операции.
english: Don't worry, everything will be fine after the surgery.

target: Заверни подарок красиво, это для особого случая.
english: Wrap the gift nicely, it's for a special occasion.

target: Улыбнись, жизнь прекрасна и полна приятных сюрпризов!
english: Smile, life is beautiful and full of pleasant surprises!

target: Сейчас ваша очередь отвечать на вопрос экзаменатора.
english: Now it's your turn to answer the examiner's question.
grammar: Ваша is feminine possessive agreeing with очередь (feminine): ваша очередь = your turn. Отвечать на + accusative = to answer.

target: Не спеши с ответом, подумай хорошенько об этом.
english: Don't hurry with the answer, think carefully about it.
grammar: Не спеши is negative imperative (imperfective): don't rush. Хорошенько means 'thoroughly/properly' (colloquial diminutive adverb).

target: Не торопитесь с решением, у вас ещё есть время.
english: Don't rush with the decision, you still have time.

target: Реставратор обновил потускневшую потолочную фреску собора.
english: The restorer renewed the faded ceiling fresco of the cathedral.

target: Проверь почту, тебе должно было прийти важное письмо.
english: Check the mail, you should have received an important letter.

target: Реши эту задачу по математике до конца урока.
english: Solve this math problem by the end of the lesson.
grammar: Реши is perfective imperative (informal): solve (this specific problem). До + genitive: до конца урока = by the end of the lesson.

target: Расскажите подробнее о вашем проекте и его целях.
english: Tell in more detail about your project and its goals.

target: Для того чтобы успеть, нужно встать рано.
english: In order to make it, you need to get up early.
grammar: Чтобы means 'in order to' and requires past tense: Я учусь, чтобы знать.

target: Положи ключи на полку, чтобы не потерять их.
english: Put the keys on the shelf so you don't lose them.
grammar: Imperative for ты: verb stem + -й/-и: читай, пиши, говори.

target: Найди ошибку в этом тексте, она где-то в начале.
english: Find the mistake in this text, it's somewhere at the beginning.

target: Возьми зонт с собой, по прогнозу будет дождь.
english: Take an umbrella with you, according to the forecast it will rain.

target: Найдите решение этой проблемы до конца рабочего дня.
english: Find a solution to this problem by the end of the workday.
Show your ticket.
grammar: Покажи is perfective imperative (informal): show. Свой agrees with билет (masculine): свой билет = your (own) ticket.

english: This way is shorter.
grammar: Короче is comparative of короткий (short): shorter. This is a simple comparative, not a superlative.

english: That road is longer.
grammar: Длиннее is comparative of длинный (long): longer. This is a simple comparative formed with -ее suffix.

english: This street is narrower.
Life is getting better.
He is significantly taller.
This neighborhood is safer.
That park is greener.
grammar: Зеленее is comparative of зелёный (green): greener. Simple comparatives can describe colors: more green.

english: His voice is lower.
grammar: Ниже is comparative of низкий (low): lower. Some comparatives have irregular stems: низкий → ниже (not *низее).

english: Her voice is higher.
This is my book.
These are my friends.
grammar: Мои is plural possessive of мой: мои друзья = my friends. Это мои друзья is a simple identification sentence.

english: This is your seat.
Her dress is new.
grammar: Её is the possessive 'her': её платье = her dress. Её doesn't change form — it stays её regardless of the noun's case.

english: Our teacher is strict.
Our apartment is big.
Their car broke down.
grammar: Их is the possessive 'their': их машина = their car. Сломалась (broke down) is a reflexive perfective past feminine.

english: Our school is new.
Your order is ready.
Whose child is crying?
grammar: Чей agrees with ребёнок (masculine): Чей ребёнок плачет? = Whose child is crying? Чей/чья/чьё/чьи decline by gender.

english: Their children study well.
I took my book.
grammar: Свой refers back to the subject: Я взял свою книгу = I took my (own) book. Use свой, not мой, when possessor = subject.

english: They invited their friends.
My mom cooks deliciously.
Their vacation starts tomorrow.
He lost his passport.
My friend likes music.
grammar: Моему is dative masculine of мой: моему другу = to my friend. Нравиться + dative: моему другу нравится музыка.

english: She helps her mom.
grammar: Своей is dative feminine of свой: помогает своей маме. Свой refers back to the subject она — her own mom.

english: Everyone loves their homeland.
She became more confident.
grammar: Увереннее is comparative of уверенный: more confident. Стать + comparative = to become more: стала увереннее в себе.

target: То ли дождь, то ли снег.
english: Either rain or snow.
Summer is warmer than spring.
The days are getting longer.
grammar: Длиннее is comparative of длинный. Становиться + comparative = to become: дни становятся длиннее = days become longer.

english: The nights are getting shorter.
He is the most prepared.
grammar: Наиболее is a formal superlative prefix meaning 'most': наиболее подготовлен = the most prepared. Used in formal/written Russian.

english: She is the least experienced.
grammar: Наименее is the opposite of наиболее: 'least.' Наименее опытная = the least experienced. Formal superlative construction.

english: He runs faster than me.
grammar: Быстрее is simple comparative of быстро (quickly): faster. Меня is genitive — replaces чем: быстрее меня = faster than me.

english: Russian is harder than English.
He is the smartest student.
grammar: Который agrees in gender/number with the noun it refers to, but takes case from its role in the clause.

english: This method is more effective.
grammar: Более эффективный is a compound comparative: more effective. Более + adjective is used when -ее comparative doesn't exist or sounds awkward.

english: She is happier than before.
grammar: Счастливее is comparative of счастливый: happier. Чем раньше = than before — comparing to a previous state.

english: She runs faster and faster.
grammar: Всё + comparative = 'more and more': всё быстрее = faster and faster. Всё intensifies progressive change.

english: We write to our friends.
It's fun with my friend.
I read yesterday a task.
grammar: Perfective describes completed, one-time actions: Я прочитал книгу.

english: The deepest lake is Baikal.
Her children go to school.
My sister lives in Moscow.
We sold our old car.
My brother has a dog.
My sister has a cat.
grammar: У моей сестры: моей is genitive feminine of мой. У + genitive + есть = possession: my sister has a cat.

english: What happened cannot be changed.
She is more patient than mom.
She is a tiny bit faster.
This is a more comfortable armchair.
She dances the best of all.
grammar: Лучше всех = best of all — superlative with genitive plural всех. Танцует лучше всех = dances better than everyone.

english: This cake is the most delicious.
The milk is warmer than usual.
grammar: Теплее is regular comparative of тёплый: warmer. Чем обычно = than usual — comparing to the norm.

english: He is richer than his neighbor.
The TV is louder than necessary.
grammar: Громче is comparative of громкий: louder. Чем нужно = than necessary — comparing to what's needed/appropriate.

english: This is the most important question.
grammar: Наиболее + adjective = formal superlative: наиболее важный = the most important. Used in formal/written Russian.

english: This is the least difficult task.
My female friend likes to dance.
Without my permission it's not allowed.
Opposite their school is a store.
The store is open since morning.
The longest river is the Volga.
He is more attentive than before.
grammar: Более внимательный = more attentive (compound comparative). Чем раньше = than before — comparing to a past state.

english: The music is quieter than desired.
The days are shorter and shorter.
She takes care of her children.
grammar: Своих is prepositional/genitive plural of свой. Заботиться о + prepositional: о своих детях = about her (own) children.

english: One's own home is the best.
She is used to her room.
Instead of tea I want coffee.

target: Самый высокий дом на этой улице.
english: The tallest building on this street.

target: Она такая же умная, как мама.
english: She is as smart as mom.
All that glitters is not gold.
The river is deeper than the lake.
grammar: Simple comparative: add -ее/-ей to adjective stem: красивее (more beautiful).

english: The mountain is higher than the hill.
Moscow is more beautiful than all cities.
The air is fresher outside the city.
The bridge is stronger than they thought.
The wall is thinner than it seemed.
grammar: Тоньше is comparative of тонкий: thinner. Чем казалось = than it seemed — comparing to perception. Стена is feminine nominative.

english: The task is harder than I thought.
grammar: Сложнее is comparative of сложный: more difficult. Чем я думал = than I thought — comparing reality to expectation.

english: The most beautiful girl in the class.
A clean lake is behind the forest.
Near our house there is a park.
grammar: Около + genitive: около нашего дома = near our house. Нашего is genitive masculine of наш, agreeing with дом.

english: The teacher whom everyone respects is leaving.
grammar: The case of который depends on its role in the subordinate clause, not the main clause.

target: Женщина, которой я помог, поблагодарила меня.
english: The woman whom I helped thanked me.
grammar: Которой is dative feminine of который: женщине, которой я помог = the woman whom I helped. Case depends on role in subordinate clause.

target: Причина, по которой он опоздал, понятна.
english: The reason he was late is understandable.

target: Кто рано встаёт, тому бог подаёт.
english: God helps those who get up early.

target: Поезд, на котором мы ехали, опоздал.
english: The train we were on was late.
grammar: На котором is prepositional of который: поезд, на котором мы ехали = the train on which we rode. Preposition + который.

target: Я помню свой первый день в школе.
english: I remember my first day at school.
This is the worst movie of the year.
grammar: Худший is a special superlative of плохой (bad). Unlike самый плохой, худший is a single-word form: the worst.

english: He is the best student in the group.
grammar: In spoken Russian, что (that/what) sometimes replaces который in informal relative clauses.

english: The quieter you go, the further you'll get.
grammar: Тише...дальше: this proverb uses comparatives in a correlative pair. Тише = more quietly, дальше = further. A folk wisdom structure.

english: The children to whom we read fell asleep.

target: Автор, чья книга стала бестселлером, приехал.
english: The author whose book became a bestseller arrived.

target: Она нашла место, где можно отдохнуть.
english: She found a place where one can rest.

target: Друзья, благодаря которым я выучил русский.
english: The friends thanks to whom I learned Russian.
grammar: Который changes by gender, number, and case: который (m), которая (f), которое (n), которые (pl).

target: Чем раньше встанешь, тем больше успеешь.
english: The earlier you get up, the more you accomplish.

target: Учёный, чьи работы известны, получил награду.
english: The scientist whose works are known received an award.
grammar: The case of который depends on its role in the subordinate clause, not the main clause.

target: Это мой дом, я живу здесь уже десять лет.
english: This is my house, I've lived here for ten years already.
grammar: Instrumental with между means 'between': между нами (between us).

target: Мальчик, чья мама — врач, хочет стать врачом.
english: The boy whose mom is a doctor wants to become a doctor.
Your package arrived.
Take your things.
Respect your parents.
grammar: Свой means 'one's own' and refers back to the subject: Я люблю свою маму.

english: Tea or coffee?
Remember your promises.
grammar: Помни is imperative of помнить (to remember). О + prepositional: о своих обещаниях = about your promises. Своих agrees with обещаниях.

english: Watch your health.
grammar: Следить за + instrumental = to watch/monitor: за своим здоровьем = your health. Свой refers back to the implied subject (ты).

english: Goodbye until tomorrow!
This is my window.
Is this your backpack?
Is this your pen?
Are these your glasses?
Our assignment is difficult.
Our neighbors are kind.
Your opinion is important.
Whose umbrella is this?
grammar: Чей это зонт? = Whose umbrella is this? Чей agrees with зонт (masculine). Это is a demonstrative: this.

english: Whose bag is this?
grammar: Чей/чья/чьё/чьи means 'whose': Чья это книга? Whose book is this?

english: Whose coat is this?
Whose gloves are these?
Whose decision is this?
grammar: Чьё is neuter of чей, agreeing with решение (neuter): Чьё это решение? = Whose decision is this?

english: He loves his job.
My parents are retired.
She found her keys.
grammar: Свои is plural of свой: she found her (own) keys. Свой refers back to the subject она — distinguishing 'own' from someone else's.

english: They remember their youth.
Their dog barks loudly.
We miss our home.
It is three o'clock now.
His work is very important.
grammar: Его работа = his work. Его doesn't change: его работа, его работы, его работе — always его regardless of the noun's case.

english: Her cat is very beautiful.
Our city is very beautiful.
My parents like to travel.
grammar: Instrumental with за means 'behind': за домом (behind the house).

english: My favorite color is blue.
grammar: Мой agrees with цвет (masculine): мой любимый цвет. Синий is a color adjective used as a noun: blue (one).

english: My favorite flowers are roses.
grammar: Мои is plural possessive: мои любимые цветы = my favorite flowers. Розы is the plural of роза.

english: His favorite hobby is reading.
Her favorite subject is math.
grammar: Чей/чья/чьё/чьи means 'whose': Чья это книга? Whose book is this?

english: This is what I need.
grammar: Что can mean 'that/which' for things: Всё, что я знаю = Everything that I know.

english: My favorite season is summer.

target: Ни он, ни она не знали.
english: Neither he nor she knew.

target: Вместо того чтобы отдыхать, он работал.
english: Instead of resting, he worked.
grammar: Вместо того чтобы = 'instead of' + infinitive: instead of resting, he worked. Чтобы here means 'in order to.'

target: Я звонил, а никто не ответил.
english: I called, but nobody answered.
grammar: А here means 'but/yet': Я звонил, а никто не ответил. А shows contrast or unexpected result, softer than но.

english: We are proud of our city.
I am proud of my achievements.
grammar: Гордиться + instrumental: своими достижениями = with one's achievements. Свой refers back to subject я.

english: She is satisfied with her job.
grammar: Довольна + instrumental: своей работой = with one's work. Short-form adjective + instrumental for satisfaction. Свой refers to subject она.

english: We are satisfied with our result.
In the morning I drink coffee.
His car is in the yard.
His parents live in the village.
grammar: Instrumental predicates: Он работает учителем (He works as a teacher).

english: Her husband works at a bank.
Our neighbors have a beautiful garden.
grammar: Свой means 'one's own' and refers back to the subject: Я люблю свою маму.

english: He takes care of his health.
They are confident in their abilities.
At whose house are you standing?
The event after which everything changed.
grammar: После которого: после + genitive of который. The case is determined by the preposition после, not the main clause.

english: He doesn't know where to go.

target: Не забывай тех, кто тебе помог.
english: Don't forget those who helped you.
grammar: Кто is used for people: Тот, кто знает = The one who knows.

target: Это именно то, что мне нужно.
english: This is exactly what I need.
grammar: Past imperfective: Я читал (I was reading / I used to read). Past perfective: Я прочитал (I finished reading).

english: His apartment is on the fifth floor.
grammar: Его is possessive 'his': его квартира = his apartment. На пятом этаже = on the fifth floor (prepositional with ordinal).

english: There are many parks in my city.
Whose car is parked at the entrance?
grammar: Чья agrees with машина (feminine): Чья машина? = Whose car? У подъезда = by the entrance (у + genitive).

english: His job takes a lot of time.
grammar: Его работа = his work. Занимать + accusative: занимает много времени = takes a lot of time. Много + genitive.

english: The people who live here are friendly.
The dog that barks does not bite.
There are things that cannot be forgotten.
The dog whose owner left is whining.
He forgot what he wanted to say.
He called to find out the news.
While we were driving, it was snowing.
grammar: И means 'and': Я и ты = You and I. А means 'and/but' for contrast: Я врач, а он учитель.

english: We will return no later than six.

target: Врач, к которому я хожу, опытный.
english: The doctor I go to is experienced.
grammar: К которому: к + dative of который. Врач, к которому я хожу = the doctor I go to. Preposition determines the case.

target: Страна, в которой мы отдыхали, красивая.
english: The country where we vacationed is beautiful.
grammar: Который changes by gender, number, and case: который (m), которая (f), которое (n), которые (pl).

target: Дорога, по которой мы ехали, плохая.
english: The road we drove on is bad.

target: Библиотека, в которую я хожу, большая.
english: The library I go to is big.
grammar: Perfective verbs describe completed, single, result-focused actions: прочитать (to read through/finish).

target: Институт, в котором она учится, престижный.
english: The institute where she studies is prestigious.
grammar: Где can replace в котором for locations: город, где я живу = the city where I live.

target: Я проснулся, потому что было шумно.
english: I woke up because it was noisy.
grammar: Потому что means 'because': Я проснулся, потому что было шумно. Потому что introduces the reason/cause clause.

target: Она говорила так, словно знала всё.
english: She spoke as if she knew everything.

target: Он всегда носит с собой свой зонт.
english: He always carries his umbrella with him.
A little boy is playing with a ball.
The city where I was born is small.
The student who passed the exam is happy.
grammar: Который сдал: который is masculine nominative — it's the subject of the subordinate clause. Сдал экзамен = passed the exam.

english: The girl whose eyes are blue is smiling.
We hurried so as not to be late.
grammar: Чтобы + infinitive = 'in order to': торопились, чтобы не опоздать. Не + infinitive = not to (be late).

english: Tell me, please, what time is it now?

target: Их любимая песня звучит по радио.
english: Their favorite song is playing on the radio.

target: Дом, в котором мы живём, старый.
english: The house in which we live is old.
The girl who is singing is my sister.

target: Парк, в котором мы гуляли, большой.
english: The park in which we walked is big.

target: Озеро, около которого мы жили, чистое.
english: The lake near which we lived is clean.
grammar: Около которого: около + genitive of который. The preposition determines the case: около которого мы жили = near which we lived.

target: Улица, на которой я живу, тихая.
english: The street on which I live is quiet.

target: Тема, о которой мы говорили, интересная.
english: The topic we were talking about is interesting.

target: Вот книга, о которой я говорил.
english: Here is the book I was talking about.

target: Мне рассказали историю, которая меня удивила.
english: I was told a story that surprised me.
grammar: Которая is feminine nominative agreeing with история: историю, которая меня удивила = a story that surprised me.

target: Мы поедем, если будет хорошая погода.
english: We will go if the weather is good.

target: Рано утром мы вышли из дома.
english: Early in the morning we left the house.

target: Учитель сказал, чтобы мы открыли книги.
english: The teacher told us to open the books.
grammar: Tense does NOT shift in Russian reported speech like it does in English.

target: Окно, которое я открыл, выходит в сад.
english: The window that I opened faces the garden.

target: Я не понимаю, о чём вы говорите.
english: I don't understand what you are talking about.

target: Друг, с которым я учился, живёт за границей.
english: The friend with whom I studied lives abroad.
grammar: Future imperfective uses буду + infinitive: Я буду читать (I will be reading).

target: Человек, у которого я спросил дорогу, помог мне.
english: The person I asked for directions helped me.
Their house is on the outskirts of the city.

target: Картина, которая висит на стене, красивая.
english: The painting that hangs on the wall is beautiful.
grammar: Которая is feminine nominative of который: картина, которая висит = the painting that hangs. Gender matches картина.

target: Человек, который стоит там, — мой друг.
english: The person who is standing there is my friend.
grammar: The case of который depends on its role in the subordinate clause, not the main clause.

target: Школа, в которой я учился, далеко отсюда.
english: The school I studied at is far from here.

target: Они горды тем, что их сын стал врачом.
english: They are proud that their son became a doctor.

target: Мало того что опоздал, ещё и забыл документы.
english: Not only was he late, he also forgot documents.

target: Либо мы идём сейчас, либо не идём вообще.
english: Either we go now or we don't go at all.

target: Вечером учитель рисует картину в студии.
english: In the evening the teacher paints a picture in the studio.
grammar: Prefixed motion verbs add direction: в- means into, вы- means out of.

target: Человек, чей дом горит, звонит в пожарную.
english: The person whose house is burning is calling the fire department.
grammar: Чей replaces которого for possession: человек, чей дом горит = the person whose house is burning. Чей declines by gender of the possessed.

target: Туман густо окутал луга и поля ранним утром.
english: Fog thickly enveloped the meadows and fields early in the morning.
grammar: Окутать means 'to envelop.' Густо = thickly (adverb). Ранним утром = in the early morning (instrumental for time).

target: Паркетчик уложил дубовые доски в большом банкетном зале.
english: The floor layer installed oak planks in the large banquet hall.
He eats and reads.
From morning till evening.
grammar: С утра до вечера = from morning to evening. С + genitive = from, до + genitive = to/until. Common time frame expression.

english: Mom dances a waltz tomorrow.
The girl washes dishes tomorrow.
He who seeks always finds.
grammar: Тот, кто = the one who: Тот, кто ищет, всегда находит. Кто is for people. This is a proverb: he who seeks always finds.

english: She remembers everything that happened.
Don't believe everything you hear.
grammar: Всему, что слышишь: что here means 'what/that which.' Не верь = don't believe (imperative). Всему is dative of всё.

english: She asked where I live.
I drink tea with milk.
grammar: С + instrumental = 'with': чай с молоком = tea with milk. С молоком expresses accompaniment/ingredient.

english: Besides Russian, he knows English.

target: Я помню то, что ты сказал.
english: I remember what you said.
grammar: То, что = 'that which/what': Я помню то, что ты сказал. Что refers to things/statements. То is a demonstrative pronoun.

target: Он ушёл, прежде чем мы приехали.
english: He left before we arrived.
grammar: Прежде чем = 'before': Он ушёл, прежде чем мы приехали. A temporal subordinate conjunction requiring a comma.

english: The flowers that he gave withered.
I am glad that you came.
grammar: Что can mean 'that/which' for things: Всё, что я знаю = Everything that I know.

english: The result we achieved is excellent.
I want to, but I can't.
He studies to become a doctor.
We left before it got dark.
grammar: Пока не = 'until': Мы ушли, пока не стемнело. Пока + не + perfective means 'before it happened/until.'

english: We will go if you want.
When she returned, everyone was happy.
Since you are here, help me.
grammar: Раз = 'since/given that' (colloquial): Раз ты здесь, помоги мне. A conversational causal conjunction.

english: Although it was cold, we walked.
Mom repeated that dinner is ready.
grammar: Tense does NOT shift in Russian reported speech like it does in English.

target: Гора, на которую мы поднялись, высокая.
english: The mountain we climbed is high.
grammar: На которую: на + accusative of который. Гора, на которую мы поднялись = the mountain we climbed. Direction requires accusative.

target: Она сделала то, о чём мечтала.
english: She did what she dreamed of.

target: Мне нравится то, как он рисует.
english: I like the way he draws.
grammar: Который changes by gender, number, and case: который (m), которая (f), которое (n), которые (pl).

target: Он ушёл, поскольку ему стало скучно.
english: He left since he got bored.

target: После того как он ушёл, стало тихо.
english: After he left, it became quiet.

target: Она плакала, потому что ей было обидно.
english: She cried because she was hurt.
grammar: Потому что means 'because': Я опоздал, потому что была пробка.

english: The song that she sings is beautiful.
grammar: Которую is accusative feminine: песня, которую она поёт = the song she sings. Accusative because it's the direct object of поёт.

english: The car that he bought is red.
grammar: Который changes by gender, number, and case: который (m), которая (f), которое (n), которые (pl).

english: The letter that I received is important.
The apartment that we rent is cozy.
The cake that mom baked is delicious.
The museum that we visited is huge.
grammar: Который changes by gender, number, and case: который (m), которая (f), которое (n), которые (pl).

english: She is satisfied with what she received.
grammar: Тем, что = 'with what/that which': довольна тем, что получила. Что refers to the thing received. Тем is instrumental.

english: While I was cooking, she was cleaning.
The librarian washes dishes at home tomorrow.
We live not far from the center.
We have been waiting since early morning.

target: Фильм, который мы смотрели, был скучный.
english: The movie that we watched was boring.

target: Река, через которую мы перешли, широкая.
english: The river that we crossed is wide.

target: Задача, которую я решил, была сложная.
english: The problem that I solved was difficult.

target: Подарок, который я получил, мне понравился.
english: I liked the gift that I received.
grammar: Что can mean 'that/which' for things: Всё, что я знаю = Everything that I know.

target: День, когда мы познакомились, был солнечный.
english: The day when we met was sunny.
grammar: Когда replaces в который for time: день, когда мы познакомились = the day when we met. Когда is simpler than в который день.

target: Он сказал то, чего я боялся.
english: He said what I was afraid of.

target: Вот дом, мимо которого мы проходим.
english: Here is the house we are passing.
grammar: Мимо которого: мимо + genitive of который. Мимо means 'past': дом, мимо которого мы проходим = the house we walk past.

target: Проблема, из-за которой он расстроен, серьёзная.
english: The problem that upset him is serious.

target: Я опоздал, потому что была пробка.
english: I was late because there was traffic.

target: Я и читаю, и пишу по-русски.
english: I both read and write in Russian.

target: Они уехали, так что дом пустой.
english: They left, so the house is empty.

target: Отец повторил, чтобы мы были осторожны.
english: Father repeated that we should be careful.

target: Он не пришёл, так как был болен.
english: He didn't come because he was sick.

target: Как дети, так и взрослые любят мороженое.
english: Both children and adults like ice cream.
grammar: Как...так и = 'both...and': как дети, так и взрослые. A paired conjunction for inclusive enumeration.

target: Хотя он был уставшим, он помог нам.
english: Although he was tired, he helped us.

target: Мне не нравится то, как он себя ведёт.
english: I don't like the way he behaves.
I used to read every day a task.
The professor who gives the lecture is famous.
The dress that she put on is blue.
grammar: The case of который depends on its role in the subordinate clause, not the main clause.

english: The place we are going to is beautiful.
The moment we were waiting for has come.
grammar: Которого is genitive masculine: момент, которого мы ждали. Ждать + genitive = to wait for. Case depends on the subordinate verb.

english: I was told that the store is closed.

target: Мост, по которому мы идём, старинный.
english: The bridge we are walking on is ancient.

target: Стол, за которым мы сидим, деревянный.
english: The table at which we sit is wooden.

target: Проект, над которым мы работаем, важный.
english: The project we are working on is important.
grammar: Над которым: над + instrumental of который. Проект, над которым мы работаем = the project we're working on.

target: Время, когда мы были счастливы, прошло.
english: The time when we were happy has passed.
grammar: Который changes by gender, number, and case: который (m), которая (f), которое (n), которые (pl).

target: Способ, которым она решила задачу, необычный.
english: The way she solved the problem is unusual.

target: Мы благодарны тем, кто нас поддержал.
english: We are grateful to those who supported us.
grammar: Imperfective verbs describe ongoing, repeated, or general actions: читать (to read, in general).

target: Праздник, ради которого мы собрались, важен.
english: The celebration for which we gathered is important.
grammar: The case of который depends on its role in the subordinate clause, not the main clause.

target: Я не уверен, что он придёт.
english: I am not sure that he will come.

target: Он молчал, будто ничего не случилось.
english: He was silent as if nothing had happened.

target: В связи с праздником магазин закрыт.
english: Due to the holiday the store is closed.

target: Страна, чья кухня мне нравится, — Италия.
english: The country whose cuisine I like is Italy.

target: Он вспомнил день, когда приехал в Москву.
english: He remembered the day he arrived in Moscow.

target: Не только он, но и она придёт.
english: Not only he but also she will come.
grammar: И means 'and': Я и ты = You and I. А means 'and/but' for contrast: Я врач, а он учитель.

target: Она не только красивая, но и умная.
english: She is not only beautiful but also smart.

target: Так как было поздно, мы легли спать.
english: Since it was late, we went to bed.

target: Я согласен, при условии что ты поможешь.
english: I agree, on the condition that you help.

target: Не то он забыл, не то не хотел.
english: Either he forgot or he didn't want to.
I will call as soon as I am free.
grammar: Imperfective future: буду + infinitive: Я буду работать (I will be working).

target: Кафе, где мы встречаемся, на углу.
english: The cafe where we meet is on the corner.

target: Как бы трудно ни было, не сдавайся.
english: No matter how hard it is, don't give up.
The garden around which there is a fence is ours.
grammar: Every Russian verb has an aspect pair: делать/сделать, писать/написать, говорить/сказать.

target: Стеклодув создал великолепную хрустальную люстру для дворца.
english: The glassblower created a magnificent crystal chandelier for the palace.
grammar: Плыть is swimming in one direction; плавать is swimming in general.

target: Переведённая книга стала бестселлером и её читали по всей стране.
english: The translated book became a bestseller and was read across the country.

target: Закрытый магазин в конце улицы раньше был популярным книжным.
english: The closed shop at the end of the street used to be a popular bookstore.
Come what may.
Without sugar, please.
Yesterday was Wednesday.
Nevertheless, we continued.
At night everyone sleeps.
He works until evening.
It snowed all night.
grammar: Сначала (first), потом (then), затем (after that), наконец (finally) order events.

english: In the evening I rest.
I think about the future.
He thinks about the future.
He is rich, however unhappy.
He came and sat down.
grammar: И means 'and' connecting sequential actions: Он пришёл и сел = He came and sat down. Two perfective verbs in sequence.

english: He is strict, but fair.
We live near the park.
grammar: Около + genitive means 'near/about': около парка = near the park. Живём is first person plural of жить.

english: Except for him, everyone came.
He came in an hour.
grammar: Через + accusative = 'in (time from now)' or 'through': через час = in an hour. Here it means 'after one hour.'

english: By evening it got cool.
grammar: К + dative for time: к вечеру = by evening. Стало + short adjective: стало прохладно = it became cool (impersonal).

english: He left an hour ago.
grammar: Час назад = an hour ago. Назад means 'ago' and always follows the time expression. Ушёл is perfective past of уйти.

english: He came despite the rain.
He either laughs or cries.
grammar: То...то = 'now...now/sometimes...sometimes': то смеётся, то плачет. Alternating actions described with this paired conjunction.

english: During class you cannot talk.
grammar: Кроме того means 'besides/moreover': Кроме того, нужно учитывать время.

english: By lunch everything was ready.
She called five minutes ago.

target: Что бы ни случилось, мы вместе.
english: Whatever happens, we are together.
grammar: Что бы ни = 'whatever/no matter what': Что бы ни случилось. Бы + ни creates a concessive clause. Note: что бы (two words) differs from чтобы.

english: The newspaper is on the desk.
The painting is above the couch.
The store is opposite the bank.
The day before yesterday it rained.
grammar: Позавчера means 'the day before yesterday.' Шёл дождь = it was raining — идти/шёл for rain in past tense.

english: He is coming from the store.
We are going to the doctor.
grammar: К + dative means 'toward/to someone': к врачу (to the doctor), к другу (to a friend's place).

english: A road goes across the bridge.
Thanks to you everything worked out.
The school is across the road.
grammar: Через + accusative = 'across/through': через дорогу = across the road. Находится = is located (reflexive).

english: Late in the evening he returned.
We are talking about our future.
grammar: О + prepositional: о нашем будущем = about our future. Нашем is prepositional masculine of наш, agreeing with будущем.

english: When I come, we will talk.
grammar: Когда + future = 'when' for future events: Когда я приду, мы поговорим. Russian uses perfective future after когда.

english: He said that he would wait.
grammar: Reported speech uses что: Он сказал, что будет ждать = He said that he would wait. Russian doesn't shift tenses in reported speech.

english: She is glad that you came.
One time he told a story.

target: Или ты, или я должен пойти.
english: Either you or I must go.
grammar: Или...или = 'either...or': Или ты, или я должен пойти. A paired conjunction for exclusive alternatives.

target: Она улыбалась, хотя ей было грустно.
english: She smiled although she was sad.
grammar: Хотя means 'although': Она улыбалась, хотя ей было грустно. Introduces a concessive clause — despite being sad, she smiled.

target: Мы пришли, а его не было.
english: We came, but he wasn't there.
grammar: А here shows unexpected contrast: Мы пришли, а его не было. А is softer than но — it notes the situation rather than contradicting.

target: В отличие от брата, она тихая.
english: Unlike her brother, she is quiet.

target: С утра до вечера он работал.
english: From morning till evening he worked.

target: На этот раз он не опоздал.
english: This time he was not late.
grammar: На этот раз = 'this time' — a fixed expression. Не опоздал = didn't be late (perfective negative past).

target: С тех пор как мы переехали, жизнь стала лучше.
english: Since we moved, life got better.
I am going to a friend's place.
I am tired, but I finished work.
I will come when I finish work.
grammar: Когда + future = 'when' for future time: когда закончу работу. Russian uses perfective future in когда clauses, not present.

english: He is smart, so he studies well.
She put the book on the shelf.
He took the keys from the table.
grammar: Со стола = from the table. С/со + genitive for 'from (a surface)': взял ключи со стола. Со is used before ст- clusters.

english: I hung the painting on the wall.

target: Если будет дождь, мы останемся дома.
english: If it rains, we will stay home.

target: Мы надеемся, что всё будет хорошо.
english: We hope that everything will be fine.
grammar: Надеяться, что = to hope that: мы надеемся, что всё будет хорошо. Что introduces the content clause after verbs of thinking/hoping.

target: Если ты придёшь, я буду рад.
english: If you come, I will be glad.
grammar: Если + future = real condition: Если ты придёшь, я буду рад. Unlike если бы (unreal), plain если describes real possibilities.
